skill.name: perplexity-search
skill.description: Search current web information with Perplexity models through LiteLLM and OpenRouter, including citations, model selection, output saving, and setup guidance.
skill.summary: Find current, cited web information through Perplexity and OpenRouter.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples, placeholders, Markdown backticks, and expected environment access. Confirmed risks include credential exposure, shell-profile modification, executable .env loading, and unrestricted output paths. Search queries are transmitted to third-party providers, so sensitive input requires review.

remediation.issue: The setup workflow exposes the API key through command arguments and terminal output.
remediation.suggestion: Read the key from a masked prompt, standard input, or an existing environment variable. Never print the complete value.

remediation.issue: Setup guidance persists secrets in shell profiles and executes .env files as shell code.
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated credential store or parsed dotenv file. Require confirmation before changing profiles, and never source an untrusted .env file.

remediation.issue: Secret files are created without enforced owner-only permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Create new credential files atomically with mode 0600, verify existing permissions, and refuse symbolic links.

remediation.issue: User-selected output paths can overwrite existing files.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict output to an approved directory, reject traversal, and require explicit confirmation before replacing a file.

remediation.issue: Complete search queries are sent to third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose provider transmission before use and prompt users to remove secrets, personal data, and proprietary content.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Accepted Through Command Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The documented setup workflow places the API key in --api-key, exposing it through process listings and shell history.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The quick-start command places a key placeholder after --api-key, and the parser explicitly accepts that secret-bearing argument.

semantic_findings.title: New Secret Files May Have Broad Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The setup helper creates a plaintext API-key file with default process permissions and does not enforce owner-only access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file is opened with the standard text write API, and no chmod or restrictive creation mode appears before the complete key is written.

content.user_title: Search the Live Web with Perplexity
content.value_statement: Static model knowledge cannot cover current research and recent events. This skill queries Perplexity through OpenRouter and returns web-grounded answers with citations.
actual_capabilities: Runs one query against five selectable Perplexity Sonar models through LiteLLM and OpenRouter.
Returns the answer, selected model, token usage, and citations when the provider includes them.
Supports model, maximum token, temperature, verbose, and output options through a command-line interface.
Saves successful search results to a user-selected file.
Includes setup checks and guides for query design, model selection, costs, and troubleshooting.
limitations: Requires LiteLLM, an OpenRouter account, a funded API key, and network access.
Sends complete queries to OpenRouter and Perplexity.
Generated claims and citations may be incomplete or incorrect and require source verification.
Provider pricing, model names, availability, and behavior may change after publication.

use_cases.title: Review Recent Research
use_cases.description: Find recent papers, reported findings, and citations for a defined scientific question.

use_cases.title: Check Current Technical Guidance
use_cases.description: Locate recent documentation, implementation advice, and ecosystem changes beyond static model knowledge.

use_cases.title: Compare Emerging Developments
use_cases.description: Summarize recent products, policies, or market changes with dated supporting sources.

prompt_templates.title: Find Current Information
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the latest reliable information about [topic]. Use sources from the past [period], summarize the answer, and list citations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for a recent topic

prompt_templates.title: Search Recent Literature
prompt_templates.prompt: Find peer-reviewed research about [question] published since [date]. Report study types, main findings, limitations, and source citations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Current Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [option A] and [option B] for [context]. Use recent evidence, explain tradeoffs, identify disagreements, and cite each major claim.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Conflicting Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [claim] across primary sources, reviews, and official guidance. Separate established facts, disputed conclusions, evidence gaps, and dated citations.

output_examples.input: What changed in AlphaFold 3 research during the past year?
output_examples.output: A dated summary of recent findings, reported benchmarks, limitations, and source citations.

output_examples.input: Compare current evidence for two diabetes interventions using randomized trials.
output_examples.output: A structured comparison of outcomes, study quality, safety findings, disagreements, and links to the cited sources.

best_practices: Include a precise topic, time range, domain, and preferred source types.
Choose the least expensive model that matches the query complexity and set a token limit.
Open important citations and verify dates, claims, methods, and source quality before reuse.
anti_patterns: Do not send secrets, personal data, unpublished research, or proprietary text in a query.
Do not treat generated summaries or citation lists as verified evidence.
Do not use advanced search models for simple facts without considering cost.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires an OpenRouter API key with sufficient account credit.

faq.question: Which model should I use first?
faq.answer: Use sonar-pro for general research. Use sonar for simple facts and sonar-pro-search for complex multi-step work.

faq.question: Does the skill access current web information?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends the query to a Perplexity model through LiteLLM and OpenRouter.

faq.question: Can it save search results?
faq.answer: Yes. The command-line tool can write successful results to a selected file.

faq.question: Are generated citations always accurate?
faq.answer: No. Open each important source and verify that it supports the associated claim.

faq.question: How should I handle sensitive queries?
faq.answer: Remove secrets, personal data, proprietary details, and unpublished material before sending a query to external providers.
